answer: One concrete mechanism: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because saffron only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, tide is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any violet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
